Hannah — ACK. Draft material attached and initial answers below; I can iterate before we send to FinSecure. Attachments: dpia_summary.docx, pseudonymization_diagram.png

Summary (high level):
- Training on customer data: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/responses to train models by default for hosted customers. Training on customer-provided content requires an explicit opt-in and contract-level permission (we document opt-ins in the DPA). Private/dedicated deployments are customer-controlled and do not feed back to Redwood model training.

- Retention: Default ephemeral retention for prompt/response logs is 30 days for Hosted accounts (used for debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring). Customers can request a shorter retention period or opt-out of retention via a flag in Console or by contract for Dedicated/Private. Retention reductions are enforced by automated TTL and deletion jobs; deletions are recorded in audit logs.

- Pseudonymization / redaction: We apply configurable redaction hooks at ingestion: standard identifier detection (PII regexes) and optional deterministic hashing for identifiers (customer-provided salt supported for Dedicated/Private). Diagram attached shows the dataflow: ingestion -> redaction/pseudonymization -> transient KV/cache -> model runtime -> short-term logs -> TTL deletion.

- Controls & evidence: We can share SOC2 Type II (redacted), CAIQ matrix, DPA+SCCs template, encryption at rest with KMS, per-route access controls, and immutable audit logs. Links: https://drive.google.com/redwood/finsecure/dpia_summary (draft).

I recommend we include the DPIA summary, the pseudonymization diagram, and the SOC2 stub in our reply. ETA: I will finalize the DPIA doc and diagram by EOD tomorrow (Aug 10, 23:59 UTC).

Hannah / Neha — technical points to include in the customer reply. Attachment: pseudonymization_algorithm_v1.txt

- Ingestion redaction: we run token-level PII detection with both rule-based (regex) and ML-based classifiers. Detected identifiers are replaced with deterministic hashes by default; hashing uses per-customer salt for Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache behavior: KV cache (prefix/cache entries) holds transient context in-memory for active sessions; persistent KV entries are never written with unhashed PII. Cache shards are rotated and TTL-bound (default 1 hour for session caches).
- Logs: request/response logs used for abuse detection include metadata-only indices and hashed identifiers. Full-text logs are TTL-managed (30-day default) and can be disabled.
- Redaction caveat: automatic redaction has false negatives with free-form data (attachments, images). For sensitive workflows we recommend Dedicated/Private or customer-side redaction prior to sending.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
